lines.beaver: 선배님, 요즘 너무 힘들어요. 시련이 왜 있을까요?
lines.beaver_en: Sunbae, things are so hard lately. Why do ordeals exist?
lines.beaver_roman: seonbaenim, yojeum neomu himdeureoyo. siryeoni wae isseulkkayo?
lines.en: I think ordeals are a treasure that helps us grow.

lines.beaver_en: A treasure? To me it just feels empty.
lines.learner: 나도 역경 속에서 허무를 느낀 적이 있어.
lines.en: I've felt that emptiness in adversity too.
lines.roman: nado yeokgyeong sogeseo heomureul neukkin jeogi isseo.

lines.beaver_en: How did you get through it back then?
lines.en: I believed in 'no pain, no gain' and set a vision.

lines.beaver_en: That's impressive. Didn't anyone help you?
lines.learner: 부모님께 도와 달라고 하지 않고 자립했어.
lines.en: I didn't ask my parents for help; I stood on my own.
lines.roman: bumonimkke dowa dallago haji anko jaripaesseo.

lines.beaver_en: On your own? That must have been hard.
lines.en: It was hard, and lonely too. But I learned.
That morality grows stronger through ordeals.

lines.beaver: 그럼 선배님은 어떤 삶이 좋은 삶이라고 보세요?
lines.beaver_en: Then what kind of life do you think is a good life?
lines.beaver_roman: geureom seonbaenimeun eotteon salmi joeun salmirago boseyo?
lines.learner: 성공하건 실패하건 간에 자율적으로 사는 거지.
lines.en: Whether you succeed or fail, you live autonomously.
lines.roman: seonggonghageon silpaehageon gane jayuljeogeuro saneun geoji.

lines.beaver_en: Where does that kind of mindset come from?
lines.en: I believe it comes from the spirit of our ancestors.

lines.beaver_en: Please say a word to the juniors.
lines.learner: 시련 뒤엔 꼭 좋은 날이 와. 끝까지 버텨.
lines.en: Good days always come after ordeals. Hang in there to the end.
lines.roman: siryeon dwien kkok joeun nari wa. kkeutkkaji beotyeo.

lines.beaver_en: You're truly a role model for us. Thank you.
lines.learner: 고마워. 너도 언젠가 누군가의 귀감이 될 거야.
lines.en: Thanks. Someday you'll be someone's role model too.
lines.roman: gomawo. neodo eonjenga nugungaui gwigami doel geoya.
